title: Budget-aware traffic steering and dashboard patterns
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview
======
This document defines a platform pattern for routing inference requests with awareness of tenant budgets and real-time cost signals, and the associated dashboard and alerting patterns that operators should use. It covers: design goals, policy primitives, implementation recipes, dashboard/Grafana panel and Alertmanager rule examples, runbook actions, ownership, and a short retrospective from pilot deployments. The intended audience is platform engineers, SREs, and product teams running heavy inference workloads.

Goals
-----
- Reduce unexpected customer spend by steering traffic when a tenant’s committed budget or burst credits are depleted.
- Maintain global SLOs for tail-latency and token throughput while applying cost controls.
- Provide clear operator visibility (dashboards/alerts) and safe automation (fallbacks, canary throttles).
- Make policy primitives reusable across hosted / dedicated / private modes.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Redwood’s multi-tenant runtime supports: hosted-api, dedicated-pools, and private deployments. Workloads vary: real-time chat (latency-critical), batch embedding pipelines (throughput-oriented), and periodic retraining/evals (cost-tolerant). Historically, sudden surge in long-running streaming generations caused high token spend and overloaded burst credits for some tenants, which resulted in manual escalations and SLA tradeoffs. The Budget-aware Traffic Steering pattern treats budget/burst credit state as a first-class input to routing decisions.

Key concepts and primitives
--------------------------
- Budget State Signal: per-tenant metrics (committed_monthly_credits, burst_credits_remaining, forecasted_spend_pct). Provided by billing+quota service and exported to metrics pipeline (Prometheus).
- Cost Weight: a runtime multiplier used by smart router to prefer lower-cost model variants (e.g., quantized family) when budget constrained.
- Priority Class: classification for requests (P0 latency-critical, P1 interactive, P2 background) attached at ingress by Auth/Client SDK.
- Fallback Policy: ordered list of compatible model variants and regions to fall back to when primary route is throttled.
- Degradation Profile: SLO-aware knobs (reduce max_tokens, switch to faster model_variant, disable streaming) applied gradually.

Design patterns
---------------
1) Signal ingestion: ensure billing service emits per-tenant gauges to Prometheus with labels: tenant_id, tier, committed_credits_usd, burst_credits. Export frequency: 60s.
2) Router decision graph: prioritize by (priority_class, budget_state, latency_headroom). Decision result: route_to=[model_variant, region], cost_weight (0.0-1.0), applied_degradations.
3) Safe automation: changes are incremental with an observable fail-safe. Every automated steering action must emit an event to events-stream (kafka) and increment a tenant-steering counter with labels for audit.
4) Policy CDN: store policy YAMLs in platform-config repo. A single policy block example below is the canonical shape.

Policy YAML (example)
---------------------
```yaml
policy_name: low-balance-steer
conditions:
  - metric: burst_credits_remaining
    operator: lt
    value: 0
  - metric: forecasted_spend_pct
    operator: gt
    value: 90
actions:
  - type: set_cost_weight
    value: 0.6
  - type: prefer_model_variant
    variants: ["gpt-small-q4", "gpt-small-fp16"]
  - type: set_max_tokens
    value: 128
audit: true
```

Implementation recipe (summary)
--------------------------------
1) Metrics: Add two Prometheus exporters: billing-exporter (per-tenant budget gauges) and router-exporter (decision labels and applied_degradations).
2) Router: Extend smart-router service to accept budget label in decision input. New input proto:
```proto
message SteeringInput {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string priority_class = 2;
  map<string,string> labels = 3;
}
```
3) Config: Add policy YAMLs to platform-config/policies/ and a reconciler service which validates and pushes to router via API.
4) Audit/logging: Emit event to kafka topic events.platform.steering and write a 30d audit log to S3 for compliance.

Dashboards and panels
---------------------
Recommended Grafana dashboards (per-tenant and cross-tenant):
- Tenant Budget Summary (vars: tenant_id):
  - Gauge: committed_monthly_credits_usd (single stat)
  - Gauge: burst_credits_remaining
  - Sparkline: forecasted_spend_pct (30d)
  - Top table: recent steering actions (last 24h) – query from kafka-backed materialized view
- Routing Decisions Overview (cluster-level):
  - Time series: steering_actions_total{action=~"set_cost_weight|prefer_model_variant"} grouped by tenant_tier
  - Heatmap: cost_weight distribution across pods (last 1h)
- SLO Impact view (per-model_variant):
  - p95/p99 latency vs applied_degradations (overlay)
  - tokens_per_second by variant

Panel configuration excerpts (PromQL)
- burst_credits_remaining for tenant_id=$tenant: `sum(billing_burst_credits_remaining{tenant_id="$tenant"})`
- steering_actions_total by action: `sum(increase(router_steering_actions_total[5m])) by (action)`
- p99 latency for variant: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_request_duration_seconds_bucket{variant="$variant"}[5m])) by (le))`

Alerts and thresholds
---------------------
Define alerts in Alertmanager grouped by severity. Examples: 
- Alert: TenantBudgetCritical
  - Expr: `billing_burst_credits_remaining{tenant_tier!="enterprise"} < 1 and forecasted_spend_pct>95`
  - For: 10m
  - Severity: page
  - Runbook: follow "Budget-critical steering runbook" below
- Alert: SteeringAutomationFailed
  - Expr: `increase(router_steering_failed_total[10m]) > 0`
  - For: 5m
  - Severity: ticket

Runbook: Budget-critical steering runbook
----------------------------------------
Objective: Minimize customer surprise while preserving availability.
1) Triage (0–10m):
  - Check Grafana tenant budget panel for tenant_id.
  - Look at steering events: `kubectl logs -n routing deployment/router --since=30m | grep "tenant=<tenant_id>"`
  - Confirm whether automated steering executed and what actions applied.
2) Immediate remedial actions (10–30m):
  - If the tenant needs emergency throughput: increase burst_credits via billing API: `curl -X POST https://billing.internal/v1/tenants/<tenant>/adj-burst -d '{"credits": 500}'` (requires billing team approval)
  - If steering is producing high latency regression: revert policy: `platform-config-cli policy disable low-balance-steer --tenant <tenant>` and notify customer success.
3) Post-incident (30m–72h):
  - Open a retro with customer success and product for billing model changes.

Safe rollout checklist for automation
------------------------------------
- Unit tests for policy parser and router decision graph.
- End-to-end test: synthetic tenant with low-balance flag and injected traffic profiles.
- Canary percent: start at 1% of traffic, increase to 10% after 24h, then 100% after 72h if no regressions.
- Telemetry: ensure steering_actions_total, steering_failed_total, and steering_revert_total are emitted.

Ownership and responsibilities
------------------------------
- Platform Router team: owns router implementation, decision API, and reconciler (primary contact: Sofia Chen).
- Observability team: dashboard templates and Alertmanager rules (primary contact: Alex Müller).
- Billing team: metrics export and burst_credit adjustments (primary contact: Priya Nair).
- SRE: incident runbook owner and oncall responder for paging.

Roadmap items and next steps
----------------------------
- Q2 2025: Add ML-driven forecaster for spend_pct and integrate into policy conditions.
- Q3 2025: Evaluate per-request token cost attribution and add fine-grained cost_weight per request signature.
- Q4 2025: Private deployment sync: provide a local reconciler that can run inside customer VPC with restricted telemetry.

Pilot retrospective (lessons learned)
------------------------------------
- What went well: automated steering reduced manual escalations by ~60% for mid-tier tenants during pilot window. Dashboards made behavioral patterns visible to CS.
- Improvements identified: need better jitter control when applying degradations (avoids synchronized latency spikes), and faster rollback primitives inside router to reduce noise.
- Behavioral note: product teams requested an "opt-out" annotation for premium customers; design approved and will be supported via policy metadata.

-------------

- /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/runtime-cost-instrumentation-and-alerting-2026

Appendix: quick commands and examples
------------------------------------
- Query recent steering events for tenant on materialized view: `SELECT * FROM steering_events_mv WHERE tenant_id='acme-corp' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;`
- Disable a policy in platform-config: `git commit -m "disable low-balance-steer for pilot" && platform-config-cli push --env prod`
- Example alert rule snippet (Prometheus rule):
```yaml
groups:
- name: steering.rules
  rules:
  - alert: TenantBudgetCritical
    expr: billing_burst_credits_remaining{tenant_tier!="enterprise"} < 1 and forecasted_spend_pct>95
    for: 10m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "Tenant {{ $labels.tenant_id }} low burst credits and high forecast"
```

Contact and escalation
----------------------
For questions or to request whitelist/opt-outs for customers, contact platform-router@redwood.com. For billing adjustments, contact billing-ops@redwood.com. For dashboard or alert changes, open a runbook PR in the observability repo and tag @AlexMuller.
